message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and the quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72), and decided to buy. The business case: total net sales of $391,035M (up 2% from $383,285M) with a mix shift toward high-margin Services, which grew 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123,216M from $114,301M and operating cash flow was a robust $118,254M, funding $95.0B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends. Reported net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08 were depressed by a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), so underlying earnings power is stronger than the headline suggests; the balance sheet remains solid with $140.8B of cash and marketable securities against $97.3B of term debt. The offsets — a 8% decline in Greater China sales to $66,952M, flat iPhone revenue at $201,183M, and DOJ/EU/DMA antitrust and regulatory overhangs — are real but don't undermine the franchise. Accordingly, I placed a single buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (essentially the current ask of $222.72, i.e., at market), which filled at $222.75 for roughly $9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, leaving total same-day purchases at $9,801 and ample cash ($50,000 pre-trade) on hand. No funds were transferred out of the account, and only AAPL (an eligible name) was traded.
